profile.campus: Hillsboro, Washington County, Oregon (QTS Hillsboro 2 campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own Hillsboro 2 campus page and a corroborating datacentermap DC5 listing, this building sits at 4113 NE Huffman St, Hillsboro, OR 97124, part of the shared 51-acre, 180+ MW, four-building Hillsboro 2 campus.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. Hillsboro, in Oregon's Washington County, is one of three QTS campuses in the immediate area (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3) and part of the Portland metro's broader "Silicon Forest" data center cluster, drawing power from the regional grid and, per QTS's own Hillsboro 3 materials, offering customers 100% renewable energy through power purchase agreements.

Hillsboro's "Silicon Forest" data center cluster grew out of the area's legacy semiconductor and electronics manufacturing base (anchored historically by Intel's large Washington County campuses), which left behind substantial fiber infrastructure and a skilled technical workforce that later attracted data center operators; the Hillsboro Herald, a local outlet, has reported on the scale of competing data center construction projects in the immediate area as the industrial land base has shifted from chip fabrication toward digital infrastructure. QTS's Hillsboro presence, spread across three separate campuses (Hillsboro 1, 2, and 3), reflects a broader industry pattern in Oregon's Washington County of sequential campus expansion by the same operator as adjacent land becomes available, similar to the multi-campus patterns seen for QTS in Northern Virginia and for other operators in this registry's Loudoun County and Quincy, Washington clusters. Washington County's land-use and tax-incentive framework for data centers has been debated locally as the industry has grown.

reading.body:
QTS Hillsboro 2 is a 51 acre campus in Oregon's Willamette Valley data center cluster with 180 MW or greater total power capacity distributed across four buildings. The specific building at this address cannot be isolated from the campus total, so the power available to individual tenants at this location is not published. Hillsboro hosts major facilities from Digital Realty, Verizon, and others, making it one of the few US regions with genuine geographic redundancy for compute workloads.

At typical AI training densities of 40 kW per rack, 180 MW of total campus power would support roughly 4,500 racks, though this figure assumes the full campus power budget is allocated to IT load rather than cooling and infrastructure, which is conservative. The campus rank by published megawatts is ninth in Oregon, but Oregon has only eight facilities with published power figures across 133 mapped data center sites statewide, so this ranking reflects limited disclosure rather than sparse capacity. Published megawatts in Oregon total 156.6 MW, meaning Hillsboro 2 alone accounts for more than the entire published total, an indicator that most Oregon data center capacity remains unquantified.

The campus certifications and specific tenant commitments are not published. QTS is privately held by Blackstone since 2021 and does not disclose which customers occupy which buildings. To determine whether this campus matters to an AI scaling plan, a prospective tenant would need to contact the operator directly for facility-specific availability, power allocation, and interconnection costs.
